question: this gene  was experimentally demonstrated to function as an E3 ubiquitin ligase through in vitro ubiquitination assays, showing self-ubiquitination capacity and isoform-specific activity (this gene.2). Its interaction with deubiquitinating enzymes UBP12/UBP13 was confirmed by pull-down and luciferase complementation imaging (LCI) assays, with ABA-induced stabilization of this gene.2 requiring UBP12/UBP13-mediated deubiquitination as evidenced by reduced protein turnover in mutants. The ligase was shown to ubiquitinate VPS23A (ESCRT-I component) via competitive binding with UBP12/UBP13, forming a regulatory module controlling ABA receptor stability and drought tolerance. Pathogen response studies revealed this gene.2's Golgi-localized promotion of Accelerated Cell Death 11 (ACD11) degradation through proteasomal pathways, while pathogen infection stabilized this gene.2 by inhibiting self-ubiquitination. Thermotolerance analyses demonstrated this gene-mediated ubiquitination of ELF3, reducing its protein levels to enhance PIF4-dependent hypocotyl elongation under warm conditions. Alternative splicing generated nuclear (this gene.1) and cytoplasmic (this gene.2) isoforms, both functional in ethylene-mediated apical hook regulation as shown by mutant complementation. Cell-free degradation assays and proteasome inhibitor treatments validated this gene.2's role in stress-induced ACD11 turnover, correlating with altered abiotic stress sensitivity in overexpression lines. Protein competition assays revealed reciprocal regulation between this gene.2 and VPS23A for UBP12/UBP13 binding, establishing a rheostatic mechanism for ABA signaling modulation.
